title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-02-28
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a 1970 show highlighted by a Lovelight sandwich, superb Mason’s Children jam and a tasty acoustic interlude.
ai_review.review: The recording is an excellent sound‑board mix that lets every instrument shine – Phil’s bass is especially clear and the overall balance is praised as “super mix.”  Musically the concert delivers strong moments: an early Lovelight → Me & My Uncle opening, a concise but gorgeous acoustic set (Little Sadie, Black Peter), a fiery Mason’s Children, and solid jams on Alligator, The Other One and China Cat > Rider.  While a few reviewers note the show never quite “catches fire” after The Other One, the set‑list flow and surprise segues keep the performance engaging.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen detailed reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4–5 stars, praising both musical highlights and the pristine soundboard recording; only a few low‑star or irrelevant comments lower the average slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with superb instrument separation; reviewers note “super mix,” “great dynamics,” and “excellent sound.” One comment mentions a short acoustic set due to monitor issues but the overall fidelity remains high.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Unusual Lovelight sandwich bookends the show, with a brief folk‑rock acoustic interlude that builds suspense before launching into electric jams; the second half features tight segues (Alligator → The Other One → Mason's Children) and a climactic return to Lovelight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: No specific critique of his playing, but reviewers reference “the last Masons? Say it ain’t so Jerry,” indicating his presence in the jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly praised for clear, “taught” bass that sits perfectly in the mix; not thumpy at all.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drum duo highlighted as “primo” and part of a “four‑armed beast Shiva dancing,” especially during the Alligator → The Other One transition.
